name: a-presentation
prompt:
Create a polished high-fidelity desktop web dashboard mockup for the existing "Idempotent requests lab". Landscape 1536x1024. This is a static DESIGN PROPOSAL, not evidence of a running application. Use the supplied screenshot ONLY as a reference for navy ink, cobalt actions, flat white/cool-gray surfaces, and readable Atkinson Hyperlegible-style sans typography. Completely replace its page composition and excessive copy. Do not carry over its hero, paragraphs, explanatory footer, large duplicated headings or split-panel card arrangement. Preserve the functional premise: a fictional maintenance request was actually saved by the server, but its reply was lost; the user's next action is retrying the SAME request, which must not create another job. Display precisely the current lost-reply stage, BEFORE retry: one send, one saved request, no client confirmation. Short English labels only, no lorem ipsum, no fake charts, no statistics unrelated to this experiment, no avatars, no marketing, no photorealistic objects, no decorative illustrations, no 3D, no gradients. Deliberate typography, generous but useful spacing, crisp restrained line icons, accessible dark text, compact calm chrome, one blue primary action. Make an implementable premium product UI, full app viewport with no device frame. Show a clear separate "Technical controls" tab. All status colors have text labels. Do not render any design explanation or annotations inside the app.
COMPOSITION A — PRESENTATION STAGE. The app is a single quiet stage for an accompanied demonstration, without sidebar. Compact 64px header: left small logo and "Idempotent requests lab"; right tabs "Guided demo" selected and "Technical controls". Beneath it a modest centered scenario switcher "02 / 06  Lost reply" with left/right chevrons. Main visual centered in the viewport, occupying the middle 55%: two simple large flat symbols, a monitor on left and a saved document on right. Label left "Your screen" and "No confirmation" in muted violet; right "Server" and "1 request saved" in green. Between them a precise thin returning arrow from the saved document toward the monitor, interrupted at its middle by a small violet break symbol. The single sentence "Saved. The reply was lost." sits just below this visual. Under that, one prominent but compact centered cobalt button "Retry same request" with arrow. Small text link "Why this works" below. Bottom edge a restrained six-segment progress navigation with only current label "Lost reply", not six descriptive texts. The focal point is the disagreement between the two labeled states and the one next action. Keep the whole screen under 55 visible words. No boxes around the two observations; the white canvas and alignment provide structure. Precise 8px button radius and fine horizontal rules, clear 24–32px heading scale, no oversized marketing title. Show the right-hand saved document with exactly one small check, never a duplicate document.
status: Unapproved static design proposal; not a running application screenshot
